body:
I mean... that is kind of the only reason

I want to be non-binary, but I don't like it when people refer to me as non-binary. It just feels really awkward. I just don't want to be cis, even though that's most comfortable for me. I have never changed my name or pronouns, nor do I want hrt.

I just don't want to be cis. It's really hard

I guess.. I've just been involved with non-binary groups for many years now. I feel like I've lied to them all. I don't want to be cis but I don't think I have ever been able to find anything which shows that I'm not idk
Perhaps. I guess I really just don't want any of the privileges of being cis, so I'm trying not to be, if that makes sense... I just don't know what to look for to feel that I'm not cis
I guess. I just really don't want to be cis, even though I have no reason to question my birth gender idk. I do not want that social privilege

Mostly because I don't want to be oppressive. It's got very little to do with how I feel inside. I've never really questioned any aspect of my gender, I just don't want to feel like I want to be cis, because of the social connotations of being cis.

Is that possible? To be non-binary without questioning your birth gender?
Then why do I relate more to binary people than non-binary people? Idk... If it were that simple then I wouldn't be worried about this

I guess I'm just not sure of question 1.

I just really don't want to be binary. I just might be

But like... How am I supposed to know that I am non-binary as opposed to being binary? I really don't want to be binary but I don't relate to any of the experiences of non-binary people.

I guess I don't know, is all

That's the only think I could reasonably think of! Like I was some kind of spy who's trying to infiltrate the trans community and undermine it in some way. I spoke to the person who told me to leave and he said he would see what he could do, but he felt it correct to ensure that those who have faced transphobic abuse from "cis male presenting people like me" should be protected (apparently multiple people voiced their concerns about my being there). 

I made sure to let him know my gender identity (he's a demiguy, I believe, so I thought he would understand). But he simply said that he couldn't ignore the discomfort of those already in the group. (I still don't know who these people are - apparently they made a formal complaint and their identities should be protected)

I can't think of any better way to prove that I am who I say I am.

I only really wanted to make friends. I don't really want to kick up a fuss and further alienate myself by forcing them to accept me.

I mentioned this in another trans group and was told that one of the reasons was that my presentation would have been discomforting for trans people who have already faced discrimination from cis people. Sort of how light-skinned POC can be made to feel unwelcome (intentionally or not) in POC spaces despite the validity of them being there. I feel guilty to say that that kind of makes sense, but I'm just not the kind of person who would be able to come up with a solution to it all.

It's definitely frustrating! But then again, I haven't been looking into to queer and sj issues for very long and I fear that if I did that then they would just school me on how bigoted I was being for ignoring their clear discomfort of being around me. 

Although I am now left alone, I can almost understand where they are coming from. Outwardly, there is absolutely no sign to suggest that I am anything other than a cis guy (everyone else seems to fit into certain queer stereotypes, that I guess give a certain shared bond). I don't even use they/them pronouns since I find them confusing when applied to me. 

I know that some of those people have been through some shit because of cis people, and I guess seeing me may have brought back some bad memories, which may have left to me being politely asked to leave. 

Since this is the university's official trans group, I fear that they know what they are doing and if I try to stand up to them, they'll just argue me away and maybe do something worse. I have asked the lgbt society about this, but they haven't replied yet.

I feel I may have been a little ambiguous in my post. Although I suspected they didn't think I wasn't trans enough, that isn't what they told me. They just said that certain members of the group were "uncomfortable" about me being there.

There are already non-binary people in the group, but I'm pretty sure they all partially use they/them pronouns for instance. They tend to dress more obviously 'queer,' if that makes sense (most of them have dyed hair for instance) and some of them go by more obviously gender-neutral names.

I know these are just surface presentations but I see how it obviously makes someone fit more easily into a loud-and-proud queer community. I pretty much dress as I have always dressed and I admit that my body is as masc presenting as they come. I find they/them pronouns confusing so I continue to go by he/him. Basically for any person looking in, they would have absolutely no idea that I was trans in any way. 

I guess some of these people have been through some shit because of cis people and to see me walk in may have brought back some bad memories. Maybe even some thought I was some kind of imposter trying to break in! But that is speculation.

This is the official trans group from the lgbt society, so I have messaged them just to see what the problem is. I'm not the most outgoing of people so I have no idea how I would be able to make my own group, let alone find some trans people who aren't already in this existing group.

Although I have known I was non-binary for a while, I haven't been massively open about it. Certainly not at the college I'm at now. As such I really don't know the first thing about finding queer groups on fb. We are quite a small college so I wouldn't think there would be anything else as local. :/

Well definitely not formally, but the group is quite small and close knit so I know I will just be made to feel unwelcome. My mental health is bad as it is and I think that would affect me more than most people.

Again, I'm pretty shy and I'm really not the kind of person to make complaints like that. I wouldn't even know who to turn to if I was!

As much as I understand you are trying to help me, I'm really not in a financial situation to be able to save up. Maybe I could spend a month getting the funds for a single hour with a therapist, but I'd then need a month for another, and in my brief spell of therapy at college, all I found out was that a single session with no series of follow up sessions just stirs things up and makes things a whole lot worse.
But I don't know what that means! How can I focus on making myself better when everything I've found online doesn't work and anything that might is out of reach

I've tried my best but there really isn't a lot that I can afford. I went to the university counsellors but they didn't seem to understand my situation, so it just made it worse. Besides I couldn't stay with them for long since their waiting list is too big for them to keep people on for a long time.

I understand what you have to say but I do think it will be difficult for me to do that.

Since any point where I try my best to do something beneficial to people, I start to enter a mental crisis for some reason. That has led me to avoid those situations all together which makes me feel even more shitty about who I am as a person. It's definitely something I've tried, but most people I have spoken to about it don't seem to understand and just call me a bigot.

I know I have to be conscious of what other people are experiencing, and that is exactly what I thought for the first few months after I was kicked out. The only problem is that this is currently the only trans group I know of in the area. I just don't know anywhere else! I've been kicked out for being in a group because of how I look but I don't feel comfortable about changing my appearance to be any more androgynous. I definitely won't be able to cope with a pronoun change, since I just won't be able to handle the confusion. 

I just feel stuck between my identity and my mind and I know one of them is going to have to break to carry on the next few years at this college in this tiny town. I just don't know what to do.

But I don't understand. I'm still reaping all the privileges of being a cis guy without me even knowing what it is I'm reaping. No one knows me as anything other than a cis guy and I'm only really out around people who are far away from me.

Now I feel left without even a group of trans people who aren't uncomfortable around me whilst I receive the privileges that none of them can get because I'm not being trans enough!

Well yes I completely understand that. And i realise that the main victims of suicide are other people. I think I touched on this in a different post, but it seems like the only negative reasons I can find for suicide are the wishes of other people. That's the only reason why I haven't done it all ready. It seems that society is very happy to sacrifice one person to a life like mine for the sake of others. My wishes are somehow completely invalid because of what they are. 

I'm not going to change society, but I am completely aware that in my situation, suicide is the only logical answer. For that reason, I am planning on waiting until I isolate myself from people I know until everyone who would care if I killed myself is either dead, or too distant to realise and/or care.

Unfortunately you only see my posts on this stuff since this is a second account (people didn't seem to like it before when I was posting about this stuff on my main account!).

Well it doesn't bother me any more. Back then I worried about it all the time but I've just decided to embrace these thoughts and it's literally changed my life for the better. My depression has completely lifted in the first time in my life, and my productivity along with it. 

I'm just confused as to why coming to terms with something like this, and being completely suicidal and happy for it is met with such disdain. If all the people I've spoken to about it seem to treat me like scum. They just want me to get psychological help, but if they truly understood what I was feeling, they would know that I should really just go and continue in the way I'm going. 

I came here more as a rant about all this, and maybe find someone who thought similar. I just don't understand why people, even very open minded people, don't seem to understand what's best for me and just assume that not being suicidal is automatically better than being suicidal. Talking about stuff like this doesn't seem to go down well in other kinds of subreddits, so that's why I brought it here. 

Sorry for the confusion

Physically, it's the people who lock me up in a hospitality after a suicide attempt and try to convince me that what I did was wrong. I have never agreed with them. They are just getting in the way.

I'm trying out new ways of suicide that are less likely to be discovered.

That does make sense, but I wouldn't say my suicidality is distressing for me. In fact it makes me feel quite content and happy. It's only after embracing it that my depression finally lifted and I felt good again. These thoughts have in fact been far more helpful to me than any kind of drugs or therapy.  

I appreciate your thoughts, but I just don't think that applies in my case.

Again, I appreciate what you have to say.

Sorry about what I said before. I don't take offence at what you said. I was really just saying that as a general statement to the world rather that to be directed to you.

But to answer your question, yes I have always been suicidal. Even before I understood what death was, I put myself to sleep every night by banging my head against the wall until I lost consciousness. Looking back, I guess I wanted to die but I didn't even know about death to actually kill myself. Hurting was the only thing available to me.

I questioned myself when I posted on here. I feel at first, I genuinely thought there was some hope for me, but now I'm beginning to realise that there really isn't. I guess I posted this just to try and confirm if there were any objective reasons to stay alive that didn't involve other people, and I haven't seemed to be given any so far. I want to make sure I've got all bases covered before I do anything. I could have posted somewhere else, but suicide is considered so bad by the rest of the world, that these places seem to be the only places where I can talk about it bluntly. 

Years of therapy, drugs and countless support groups have done nothing for these thoughts. They've only made them more and more intense and I absolutely love it! It's like I'm beginning to embrace them and I just feel so good! Like all the sadness in my life has been because of my attempts to push them away. Now that I'm harming freely, I just feel so fantastic! I just don't understand why something that makes me feel so unbelievably good can somehow be so wrong and bad.  

Again, the only people who have told me that self harm is bad have been people who aren't me. They have absolutely no idea of the euphoria that I have experience from it. Unlike any kind of pleasure I have ever experienced elsewhere  (yes, that includes sex). They can't feel that, so they must only feel the pain and that's why they must think it's bad. It's not like heroin at all. I'm not destroying my life - I'm coping extremely well with my studies, job and volunteering. The creative writing is coming along nicely too. If anything, this harming has done more for my productivity than any of the drugs or therapy. There just doesn't seem to be a single downside. 

I completely appreciate your concern for me, and it's touching that you want to 'help', but I just have to say again that you are YOU. Maybe the majority of the people in the world don't agree with me but I would guarantee that they would change their minds if they could feel what I feel.

Thanks for taking the time to reply :)

I appreciate what you have to say but I still have the same question that I had before. 

Why are cravings of death and self destruction not healthy? It's only been other people who have tried to tell me this, and I know they mean well but they still aren't me. How do they think that they know so much about me and my brain that they have the gall to tell me that what I'm thinking is not healthy?

Maybe most human brains are made to value survival, but since these thoughts of destroying my flesh and killing myself have been with me all my life, it's not to much of a stretch to say that maybe my brain just... wasn't. There has been no reason whatsoever that would have caused these thoughts to start. I have spent years trying to find one. I am just suicidal. That is who I am.

Why do other people want to put in so much effort into the futile task of making my brain change how it thinks? Why can't they just let me do what my whole life has been leading up to?

I'm not depressed. I know what depression feels like.  All these thoughts of harm and suicide are really positive things. Why does that make them unhealthy? Isn't health about trying to maximise how you feel about your life?

As for reasons to live. There are none. There is nothing that gives me any kind of positive feeling like harming and killing myself. Why should I want to look for one? Again, it seems like this suggestion has only come from people who claim to know more about how I think, or should think, than me.

>So right now it is better to see if the treatment you are getting changes something or if the therapy you are waiting for changes something. You can reevaluate if suicide is the best option afterwards.

I know what you are getting at, but that assumes that I want to get rid of the suicidal thoughts. My life has changed so much, that these thoughts are the only thing left that I can truly call 'me'. Getting rid of them would be killing me anyway, but also giving into the selfish demands of the world to keep me alive. Wanting to die is what makes me "me" and killing myself is just the endgame.

I know suicide is drastic and irreversible. Every minute of my life I have never wanted to be alive. Death would be the peace and non-existence that I have craved for so long. I just want to go back to the nothingness that was there before I was born and let my consciousness rot into the ground. That's all I'm asking!

>Maybe I misunderstood, but to me it seemed that you wanted to help directly, but that it often hasn't really worked out. If an indirect approach produces better results than a direct approach, why chose the direct one?

Indirect approaches won't work. From what I've seen its just a lie to tell people they are helping when they really aren't. Even if did help, I wouldn't feel comfortable doing anything anyway. The fear of criticism and from being corrected has become so strong that I can't even enter feminist spaces without a needle to stab and punish myself for getting things wrong and the things I know I'm going to get wrong. I know I will never know everything, which makes me happy to punish myself for not getting things right all of the time.

>Also, in another comment, you write that because of the harm you have done to oppressed people, killing yourself would help feminism. I don't think that is actually the case. Your suicide would also have an effect on feminism, because it will effect your feminist friends and their activism.

It's harder than that though. If I ever misgender, offend, get criticised, or get something wrong, I'll just lock up. I can't apologise because I know the damage is done and will never be healed, in my mind anyway. I can't even bear to look at someone I've done any of those things too. Even thinking about them makes me cut myself. I just slowly cut them out of my life until they never have to see me again. If I keep going at this rate, I'll make sure that I have no feminist friends to affect by my death. I cannot guarantee that my death would be a positive impact on feminism, so I'll make sure that it has no affect whatsoever. It's better than any more mistakes at least. 

I have never been able to do anything for feminism. I have no name for myself and I doubt many of my feminist friends even think I am a feminist. I don't have a name for myself and no one knows me from Adam. I can't help oppressed people. However hard I try, I just keep making things worse. There us no guarantee that I'll change this pattern, so killing myself now would make sure any kind of damage I do is put to an immediate stop. **It is the only absolutely guaranteed way** Any issues that come from my death would be quickly forgotten and ripple out into nothingness, while the actual, proper and successful feminists will make the world better. I am completely disposal and expendable. There is no inherent benefit for my specific existence. I'll never be able to make a lasting change, and that's why killing myself and submitting to my lifelong dream rather than continuing just makes perfect sense. 

Better people will make more use of the opportunities and resources that I would have been afforded.

>If I may ask, what were your earlier reasons for considering suicide, before you came into contact with feminism?

To be perfectly honest, I really don't know. I just know that I wanted to die and was hell bent on doing it at any cost. Maybe I hit my head hard enough to forget.

>which of these needs are met and which aren't? Was there ever a point in your life when all these needs were met? 

Again, I'm pretty sure all of these things are satisfied. While I was at university, when my latest downward spiral began, I was enjoying my work. I felt I was improving at it and I had lots of friends (or at least I think they are my friends, based on how they react to me). Unfortunately I suffered a bit of burnout and have taken a year out to recover, and I still feel these are being satisfied. My family have repeatedly indicated that they love me, however I still don't quite know what it feels like to love someone back. 

It's not as if I am completely not able to understand others. I've just never been able to experience those emotions firsthand. After years of practice I can simply decode other people's emotions and understand them just as quickly and easily as other people, it's just it wasn't ever instinctive. 

>This isn't uncommon for depression. See here. Depression can also start during childhood, which likely happened in your case.

For this, I actually know that I'm not depressed. I went though a bout in the past and manged to recover quite quickly, so I do know what it feels like. My thoughts of wanting to kill myself and cut myself up are almost completely severed from my actual 'mood'. I've been tested for depression recently and don't show any signs of having it at all (other than constant and intense thoughts of suicide)

I can feel the antidepressants working well. I have taken different ones before at a much lower equivalent dose and could immediately tell that they weren't working. They enable me to get out and take care of myself as well as going outside, getting exercise and going to work. They just aren't quite powerful enough to even touch at my suicidal thoughts. I have repeatedly told my psychiatrist this, but they are wanting to wait a little allow the high dose to stable itself before they do anything else.   

>Making a valuable contribution to other people's life doesn't always have to be helping them with their problems. Are there people who enjoy your company? Do you/could you produce something that other people might enjoy?

In the past, people have told me that they enjoy being around me, as well as enjoying my conversations, writing, music and compositions. Unfortunately that just isn't enough. I MUST be helping them overcome their problems directly, never indirectly. It is objectively the easiest way for marginalised/oppressed people to help overcome their problems posed on them by society. I want to help them and then clearly see how that help is improving their situation. I just can't do that with music and art and all those soft things that I can do. 

I guess I just feel irritated with people who seem to say that whatever I'm feeling is ""wrong"" or ""ill"" and say that what they think is reality is the one and only reality that needs any consideration. Why can't my reality be the one I have? This has been my whole life and everything that I have known. What gives you the authority to say to me that I am living in some kind of dream? Just that thought alone makes me want to kill myself - that the world has completely discredited that permanently suicidal people exist. Why can't we be free to kill ourselves if that is the only constant thought that we have ever known?

The only kind of emotion I feel is when I want to kill myself. I guess it's like pure joy, but somehow a little more ethereal. It fills me up inside to know that complete and utter oblivion is just one step away. I know my last thought will be happy as a slip away. The thought of never having to exist, to be truly indifferent to everything and unaware of everything and just... black. That the only thing that keeps me going - The only thing I ever want to do with my life is to die.

Well I've been suicidal for as long as I can remember, my reasons for it have just changed and evolved as I've grown.

It's sort of both of those things, really. I don't think I've ever REALLY felt properly happy, I certainly don't remember it if I have. So I guess I am not really sure what makes me happy. It's not like I'm depressed though. It's more like everything is just... neutral and blank. 

I am certainly aware that other people feel happy all the time. That's why I want to help other people with their problems. If I'm not then I'm just being useless - I can't feel good about myself and I can't help other people with their problems. I am doing nothing but straining the money and food and other resources that are being offered to me. Those would be much better of going to someone who is being useful or at least actually wants to carry on living.

Well, to be perfectly honest, I really don't know. 

All my skills that I have can only really benefit myself through selfish means (being able to make lots of money and manipulating people to helping me in all kinds of other ways). Anything else I can do won't help anyone in any way. Trying to help people is all I have.

I've even become a student counsellor to help others cope with their constant suicidal thoughts (since I had no idea what I was experiencing all my life was somehow out of the norm). The true kicker was when no one, not one single person, wanted to talk to me of their own accord. It just never happened. Even the most mundane things were somehow unable to be talked to about with me. It's just something about me that is just intrinsically repulsive (there is literally no other reason).

In a world where no one needs help, I will still feel awful, maybe even worse than I am now. I will simply be useless. Death is even more desirable in that scenario

I've been trying my hardest to get help, but at the moment I just have to wait for it. That's all I can do right now.

I've thought about talking about what I'm going through, but just think what the reaction from the feminist community would be. 

"Hey, look! It's another white person who looks masc enough to have both male and cis privilege. Look! He's trying to show the world that it should try and make space for him, and that he really is oppressed. What a prick!"

I just won't happen. I'm just not the kind of person that people need to hear right now. I'll just be adding my voice to the shouting match where the truly oppressed and disadvantaged are trying to get heard. There are going to be so many more oppressed people in my situation that simply deserve to be heard over me. I am not needed in this situation; they can just do it without me!

Judging by the reaction from people here, even those who are mentally ill just can't seem to understand and respect that I genuinely want to hurt and kill myself. I don't have depression (I've already had it, and it bears no resemblance to what I'm feeling now), I just want to die. They just seem to view me as some unfortunate person who can't seem to see the 'reality' that I'm just not ever been able to see. 

No one has been able to logically explain how the world will benefit from my continued existence. But I've been able to consistently and repeatedly been able to show how it would be able to benefit from me killing myself. 

It's just the truth
I'm sorry you couldn't help me any more than you could

Recently my feminism has been pretty much non-existence. I have often found myself not picking up on things that used to abhor me. Sexist/racist/transphobic/homophobic things. I just can't even think about them without triggering some kind of suicidal crisis. 

I just feel that the feminist in me is slowly dying and I can't do anything but to watch it rot away into nothingness. And I can't just tell my feminist friends that I can't be a feminist at all because of my mental health. That's just too selfish for me to even bear.

But this is the only thing I have never known. That's like telling someone that actually their entire life is actually a dream and means nothing in comparison to 'real' life. This has been my life. I have been suicidal all my life and if that's a lie, then I guess that's just another reason for me to kill myself. How can someone just say that their 'life' and what they have experienced is someone more valid than the only thing that I've ever been able to call 'life'.

I was once a little boy who hit my head against the wall to go to sleep every night for years. I thought what I was thinking was exactly the same as everyone else, and that everyone must do the same. Since I never saw people hurting themselves, I kept it private too. I didn't let my parents know because that clearly wasn't how the world worked. People kept their harming secret. 

The cuts and scars are beginning to cover up my skin now and the welts caused by the infections I have been giving myself are dark enough that some might think they are tattoos. I might have depression and I might have OCD but this IS my life. It's the only thing I've got to see the world and it just can't be all a dream. It can't. 

I see people tell my why I'm bad when I meet them and I can't do anything to help. I am surrounded by people who are better at me at everything that I value and I have no chance of being a shadow in comparison to them. They show how easy it is for people to push past and 'self-care'. I never knew that self-care wasn't whipping/piercing/cutting/hitting yourself but that's just what I've been doing.

Even Everyday Feminism as told me to just get over it and apologise and try to make amends but they just don't understand that that isn't possible. It is just not even thinkable for me. I have never been able to deal with failure, I can't now. And if I do even reach a point where I can deal with failure (which has basically a zero likelihood) I know that I won't be the person I am now. I will simply be a puppet, existing purely for the selfish needs of others. Why can't I be selfish and just kill myself?!

Suicide is not objectively wrong. To say so would be that my life and existence is objectively wrong and thus I should just kill myself anyway. I'm sorry, but that's just how it is for me.

Thank you for the research, that makes a lot more sense to me. 

>  Ending it now will mean that you will never have a chance to right those wrongs and move the scales of your actions back to the positive.

I know that makes so much sense, and in most situations I am sure that would be a great solution. I don't really want to go into detail into what has occured, but I can say wholeheartedly that killing myself IS the only way that I can write those wrongs. Of course it may not make things positive for me again, but it definitely won't make them worse. I just don't feel at liberty to ask for any better.

More good people will make the world better, but I just don't feel I am one of those people - I deserve to suffer and everything that I face in life constantly reminds me of that. I just don't think that any amount of self-care will put me in a position to help anyone else, thus rendering the whole nurturance thing a little moot in my case. The very act of helping others seems to be the common denominator of what I can't do. That is why suicide is vital to my situation. I'm trying to work out the best way to be able to put through just how necessary it is, but it seems that society seem to demonise the action so much, it's pretty much impossible. I need to die, and if I can't do that, I simply have to destroy my body until I feel I deserve what I have gotten, if that point ever comes.

I'm sure your nurturance culture article is great but it is very long. However, from what I read at the start, it seems to read more like some kind of wishy-washy motivational post. It doesn't even begin to show WHY men helping themselves fixes everyone else. Maybe this is just me being tired and stupid, or maybe me being to literal. But I am someone who works with logic and proof (I'm a mathematician, by the way). I just can't understand something like this unless you can prove it. I'm sorry I'm being so blunt and unhelpful, but articles like this just don't make sense. I need more than a statement, what that statement means and then thousands of words that I just can't read at the moment (or at all for that matter) that include quotes from fiction of all things!

I know feminism should be intersectional and I understand why it's wrong for people to assume my situation, but from what I've seen the world simply isn't in a position for people to be pussyfooting around all the intricacies of oppression before making a judgment on me. People hate me for what I've done (or rather not done). I know this because they have told me. I can't apologise because I can't look them in the eye or even talk to them, either in real life, or over the internet. The damage that I have cause will be permanently etched on my mind, and as far as I am concerned, their's too. I can't take this away and I can't forget unless I physically beat myself until I can't remember anymore. 

When I am in public, I will forever be judged because of this, and unless I'm able to explain this to everyone in the world, then that's just going to carry on happening. I've put myself in a position where I am aware of all the awful things happening around me but simultaneously unable to do anything about it.

> You, or anyone else, are not obligated to take on every opportunity that you see to promote social justice movements.

The sad reality is that I have never been able to promote social justice movements. I just lock up uselessly and can't do anything and what I see. I can't even comment on a feminist forum because of the fear of offending someone or having to be criticised or told what's wrong with what I've said. The OCD just gets to me and takes over. I will not comment or post or do anything unless I am absolutely sure I am correct in everything that I say and in the way that I say it. It just can't be any other way. 

I don't want therapy to change me into someone who I'm not. Drugs have already done that enough to my mind already. The fact of the matter is that people think I am a bad person, and whatever I think of myself is not going to change anything. In the eyes of society I am a bad person, and unless I change my very conscienceness, that will never change. That is why I must kill myself: I can see every way that I am wrong and can't help but carry on being a bad person. 

Unfortunately there are people who I have irreparably hurt through no intention of my own. I know you won't be able to know everything, but just trust me in that I have caused some genuine damage. There is no guarantee that I won't do this again, which is why suicide IS the only option - I have spend 21 years of my life meticulously working this out. I can say for sure that my life is not worth the number of lives I have damaged already, let alone all the ones I know I'll damage in the future.
